parsed.explanation: The combined regime shows no documented traveler-facing restriction: no criminalisation of gender expression, no facility, document, custody or care exposure, and no trans-specific police or state action. Anti-discrimination covers sexual orientation only — a resident-side gap, not a visitor exposure, since no instrument is shown reaching trans travelers. Social record: documented harassment dated 2004-2007 (none since, which the dossier itself cautions proves nothing), a religious brake, and a 'tolerant as long as it's not in their face' norm — friction rather than threat-framing. Offsetting positives are real: functional parliament/courts, civil society, LGBT venues, tourism positioning, and a kingdom-level 2015 endorsement expressly including transgender persons. Thin trans-specific data caps the score below the low-risk band.

entry_documents.exposure: No document, marker, screening or entry-friction rule for trans visitors is documented.
entry_documents.protection: Wider-kingdom framework endorsed equal LGBT rights including transgender persons (2015); no entry restriction cited.
entry_documents.interaction: Not_documented — whether document mismatches trigger secondary screening at the territory's or parent's border is unanswered.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No arrest, detention or custody practice targeting gender-nonconforming visitors is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Same-sex conduct legal; anti-discrimination code (2012) with fines to one year imprisonment, though grounds are orientation-only.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Not_documented — no record of how police would treat an outed trans visitor.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No facility-access, ward-placement or birth-sex rule is documented at territory or parent level.
federal_state_facilities.protection: None documented specifically; kingdom framework endorsement is a climate signal only.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Not_documented — parent kingdom's facility rules, if any, are not stated.

care_services.exposure: No care denial, medication seizure or HRT restriction documented.
care_services.protection: Registered partnerships grant emergency medical decision rights (2016); no trans-specific care protection cited.
care_services.interaction: Not_documented — emergency care treatment of an outed trans visitor is unanswered.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Historical official opposition to LGBT rights (government opposed 2004-2007 court challenge); youth stigmatised as 'disordered' per territory's own 2015 acknowledgement.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Parliament passed partnerships 11-5; supreme court of governing state imposed marriage equality 2024; anti-discrimination statute on books.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Documented societal/official friction is dated; no record of state threat-framing toward trans visitors specifically.

minors_guardians.exposure: No findings on minors' services, schools or documentation; territory acknowledged conservative norms and stigmatisation of LGBT youth.
minors_guardians.protection: Age of consent 16 equal for both orientations; same-sex adoption legal (resident-facing).
minors_guardians.interaction: Not_documented — a trans child's documents, facilities or care in transit are unanswered.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Rocks thrown at a lesbian couple and frequent harassment documented during 2004-2007 litigation; no later incident documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Active civil society: three equality organisations, gay bars, LGBT-friendly venues, tourism positioning as safe and welcome.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Dated single-pattern harassment; dossier explicitly warns absence of later cases is not evidence of absence.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Gender identity absent from enumerated discrimination grounds — no trans-specific remedy documented; harassment record thin and dated.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning institutions: courts imposed recognition, parliament legislated, petition of ~20,000 acted on; orientation-based anti-discrimination penalties exist.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse machinery works for orientation; extension to gender identity is an open question, not a documented denial.

anchor_checks.comparison: No Visitor-Conduct-style register, entry bar or universal administrative exclusion exists here; nothing in the dossier reaches every trans traveller. Far above 0.35-A: no state exclusion regime, no unappealable adverse decision documented.

Similar in that discretion and uncertainty remain (orientation-only protections, unanswered document screening), but 0.55-B has documented secondary screening and denial of entry under discretionary grounds. Here no such border friction is documented, so higher than 0.55-B.

0.75-C has trained border staff, tribunal appeal, brief detention risk and explicit document-mismatch handling. This dossier documents no trans-specific border or detention episode at all and thinner formal recourse for gender identity, placing it a step below 0.75-C.

0.85-C shows care guarantees with working ombuds enforcement. Here no trans-specific protection or enforcement record exists — only orientation-based law and climate signals — so clearly below the 0.85 tier.

parsed.synthesis: The operative system combines a permissive parent framework (2015 kingdom endorsement expressly including transgender persons; supreme-court-imposed marriage equality) with a local regime that is silently silent on gender identity rather than hostile to it. No traveler-facing restriction — entry, documents, facilities, custody, care — is documented on any level, so the heaviest exposure tiers are absent rather than merely unreached. What remains is social: dated 2004-2007 harassment, an official acknowledgement of conservative norms and youth stigmatisation, and a 'discreetly out' social contract polised largely by religious influence. That is tier-3 friction/hostility at most, with functioning courts and active civil society as genuine recourse signals. Trans-specific thinness and orientation-only protections keep the score out of the low-risk band.
